messages.author: ddfdd96edf5576c6
messages.subject: Outdated runtime files
parts:
Hi,

since I installed the latest version of the R-plugin from vim-scripts/Vim-R-plugin
using Vundle, I get a warning about outdated runtime files every time I use the R-plugin (I'm using Ubuntu 14.04 with Vim version 7.4.52). I've tried adding jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime to my plugins, but the warning remains, presumably because the system-wide runtime files (under /usr/share/vim/vim74/) get precedence over the ones in my home directory. I really don't want to replace my system-wide runtime files manually every time there is a new version on R-Vim-runtime. So my question is, is there any way to keep all parts of the R plugin up-to-date using a Vim plugin manager such as Vundle?
I'd like to add that I really enjoy using the Vim-R-plugin, it's just that I find it more and more difficult to manage all necessary files and packages on two different systems. Already now, to replicate my Vim-R setup I need to install Vim, R and tmux via the Linux package manager, vimcom and colorout via the R package manager and the Vim-R-plugin itself through Vundle. In addition, I need to make modifications to a number of dotfiles. Having to modify the system-wide runtime files adds another level of complexity. I don't want to complain, I'm very glad that I get this great plugin for free. I'm just trying to keep it working on my systems without too much hassle.

messages.author: b256a2742aacd200
messages.subject: Re: Outdated runtime files
parts:
You could try changing the order that the they are loaded by Vundle. The files of R-Vim-runtime should be read first. That is, you should have:

Plugin jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime
Plugin vim-scripts/Vim-R-plugin

Please, tell me if this solution works to you. Anyway, I added a check in the scripts to avoid the warning in this case:
https://github.com/jcfaria/Vim-R-plugin/commit/9ecae8c1d5b6c8d646dddf87f46087986ebab3e3

messages.author: ddfdd96edf5576c6
messages.subject: Re: Outdated runtime files
parts: Thank you for the quick reply. I changed the order of the plugins in my vimrc file as you suggested, but I still get the warning message each time I open an R file. With your change in the scripts that warning should no longer appear, but are the R-Vim-runtime files in my home directory read by Vim? If Vim ignores those files and uses the system-wide runtime files instead, am I likely to run into problems? The README of jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime suggests that I won't need these extra runtime files if I compile the latest Vim version from source. I would do that if it's the easiest way to ensure that the Vim-R-plugin is working correctly.

> warning message each time I open an R file. With your change in                                                                                                             
> the scripts that warning should no longer appear, but are the                                                                                                               
> R-Vim-runtime files in my home directory read by Vim?

I am not sure of what happening in your case, but I will release a
new version today that will do the command

  runtime ftplugin/r.vim

This means that if the file ftplugin/r.vim exists anywhere in
Vim's runtime path, it will be sourced and the warning will not
appear.

> If Vim ignores those files and uses the system-wide runtime                                                                                                                 
> files instead, am I likely to run into problems?

The problems depend on the files that are missing: ftplugin (the
least important), indentation and syntax highlight.

If the files are not missing but are old, you will not have big
problems, only minor issues, like = and == being both highlighted
as logical operators (the correct is to highlight = as assignment
operator).

> The README of jalvesaq/R-Vim-runtime suggests that I won't need                                                                                                             
> these extra runtime files if I compile the latest Vim version                                                                                                               
> from source. I would do that if it's the easiest way to ensure                                                                                                              
> that the Vim-R-plugin is working correctly.

Yes, if you compile Vim from the mercurial repository, the runtime
files will all be there.

You may also want to try Neovim instead of Vim:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim
It already has some advantages over Vim and is pretty stable
because the guys who develop it have added a lot of tests to avoid
bugs. And there is a PPA for Ubuntu:
https://github.com/neovim/neovim/wiki/Installing-Neovim#ubuntu
